newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds ended sharply weaker on Friday after the market had been jolted by the release of disappointing money supply data late on Thursday, dealers said.
After moving some 20-basis points higher at the opening, the key R150 bond extended its losses in the afternoon, and was last quoted at 14.915 percent from 14.60 percent overnight.

Traders said the broad-based selling was triggered by the the release of poor money supply data late on Thursday, which prompted Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals to say there was no room for a rate cut at this stage.
The data, released at 1500 GMT on Thursday, showed money supply grew 16.89 percent year-on-year in January, while private sector credit extension ballooned 17.07 percent.
The figures were above market expectations of a 15.8 percent and 15.3 percent respectively.
Foreign and local institutions as well as jobbers were in the market on Friday, traders agreed.
"The market was very nervous and stock was coming up from everywhere. Sentiment has changed a bit -- but I think this correction is good for the market," one said.
"After the local close we might see some of the U.S. players coming in and they may take out stock as well," another trader added.
Dealers said that if the selling continued, the R150 could move back above the 15.00 percent level again, while downside potential was pegged at between 15.88 to 15.84 percent in the short-term.
The rand also ended weaker, moving in sympathy with the bond market and was last at 4.4780/4810 against the dollar from 4.4650/80 overnight.
The currency started off the day at 4.4750/4780 on the dollar, after losing strength in after-hours trade on Thursday also in the wake of the poor money supply figures.
The market remained quiet through the day and in the afternoon session dealers reported limited interest with some late dollar demand seen.
"It's been dead, dead, dead. The main reason is that it's month-end and a Friday. There's a lack of any specific interest as such," one said.
Dealers said the currency was expected to test the 4.5000 level early next week. "If that doesn't work they'll go back to 4.43 but I imagine they will try the upside first," one said.
Traders believe the Reserve Bank is keen to support the currency as it approaches the 4.50 level.
Against the crosses the rand was last quoted at 7.2862/2964 on sterling from 7.2674/2767 overnight and at 0.3777/3780 marks from 0.3774/3778 previously.
On the money market, rates held unchanged between 16.50 and 16.70 percent. The 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.179 billion rand on Thursday from 9.927 billion rand on Wednesday.
Bond Exchange statistics show foreigners sold a net 100.54 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 107.81 million rands on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.3 billion rand from 7.3 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Juliette Saunders, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
